_comment: Tool policy for the self-briefing planner quartermaster.sh runs unattended.
The planner's prompt embeds a Linear ticket description — text any
workspace member can edit — and runs with nobody watching, so the policy
is deny-by-default and the allow list is deliberately tiny: everything
absent from `allow` fails immediately rather than prompting, so nothing
blocks waiting for a human who is asleep.
No Bash at all. Permission patterns match the head of a command line and
cannot see what it goes on to execute or write: an allow-listed find can
-exec anything, rg can --pre anything, and cat/jq can redirect anywhere,
which would hand a poisoned description exactly the shell a deny list
pretends to close. Research is Read/Grep/Glob; nothing more is needed to
write a brief.
No Task either. A subagent is a second context with a turn budget of its
own — the ration --max-turns exists to impose, handed out again — and it
reads the same description with none of the caller's suspicion. Whatever
a subagent could research, the planner can research itself.
Write is scoped to the runs directory under the default HARNESS_DIR — the
one mutation the planner exists to make. A non-default HARNESS_DIR makes
self-briefing fail visibly (reported as could-not-self-brief) rather than
widen this file. The deny list is belt to those braces: a rule added to
allow later cannot re-open the shell, editor, or network paths without
also deleting a deny. Scoped to runs/, not to one ticket's directory under
it — quartermaster.sh checkpoints every brief.md before the planner starts
and puts back anything it wrote outside the brief it was asked for.
The harness's own secrets are denied by path. The planner has no way to
send anything anywhere itself — the network tools are denied above — but
the brief it writes is read by an implementer whose settings do allow Bash
and WebFetch, so a secret quoted into a brief is a secret one step from
leaving the machine. These paths assume the default HARNESS_DIR, like the
Write rule; a key kept elsewhere (LINEAR_API_KEY_FILE) needs its own deny.
Read is what this closes. Grep and Glob take a search root rather than a
file path and are matched by tool name only, so treat the deny as the
brake it is, not as proof — what confines the planner is that nothing it
reads has a way out of this machine.
